title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: The briefing distinguishes the planned upload support from today's documented limitations and accurately reports the roadmap, licensing and existing controls. Two control paths reach the correct configuration page but should continue to the settings described in their rows.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support uploading MPIP sensitivity-labelled files to Copilot Studio agents deployed on the Microsoft 365 channel.
claims.quote: Unblock users from upload files with Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MPIP) sensitivity labels to Copilot Studio agents deployed on the M365 channel.

claims.quote: with label protections enforced end-to-end.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The current file-input documentation says encrypted files, including sensitivity-label encryption, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For an encrypted or password-protected Office upload, the agent can tell the user that it cannot read the protected file.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads instead produce a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The file-input article describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The file-input article points to Microsoft Copilot Chat as an experience supporting sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: or use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: Publishing and configuring the Teams and Microsoft 365 channels makes an agent available in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: This article describes the Copilot Studio process for making an agent available in Teams and Microsoft Copilot, not general plugin setup.

claims.claim: Purview's general AI guidance requires EXTRACT as well as VIEW to return content encrypted by a sensitivity label.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page documents encryption support only for sensitivity labels and the SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The SharePoint troubleshooting page differs by saying the agent cannot extract or ground on encrypted files.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The effective EXTRACT usage right determines whether Copilot or agents can display encrypted text and can differ from the label template.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents honor the EXTRACT usage right for a user, however it was applied to the content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The person applying encryption is the Rights Management owner and always retains EXTRACT.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner.

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.claim: Flows, connectors and tools can pass uploaded files to downstream systems such as SharePoint and ServiceNow.
claims.quote: Optionally, you can add logic in your flow to send this file to SharePoint, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and similar services.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an upload sensitivity-label check at the downstream tool or flow hand-off.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files tools connectors sensitivity label check EXTRACT permissions enforcement. Opened: pass-files-to-connectors; image-input-analysis; ai-copilot-studio.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents have documented access limitations for unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: A default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents is one exception.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents

claims.claim: Directly referencing a document by typing slash is another exception.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/"

claims.claim: Both exceptions require the user's EXTRACT permission.
claims.quote: (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[2].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Documented label-based Copilot DLP coverage for Copilot Studio agents is restricted to SharePoint knowledge sources.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.claim: The DLP location page says directly uploaded prompt files are not scanned for sensitive data.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort needed for agent retrieval, responses and actions.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.claim: The generative-answer feature rate is 2 Copilot Credits, subject to qualifying licensed usage inclusion.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Classic answers, generative answers and Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user when the agent uses that user's authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.claim: Purview recommends enabling sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive for labelled content stored there.
claims.quote: If you haven't already, we recommend you enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive and also familiarize yourself with the file types and label configurations that these services can process.

claims.claim: Without enabling labels for those services, accessible encrypted files are limited to data in use in Office apps on Windows.
claims.quote: When sensitivity labels aren't enabled for these services, the encrypted files that Copilot and agents can access are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.

claims.claim: The printed Purview DLP path reaches the Copilot policy location in the custom policy wizard.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
3. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
4. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct wizard page but stops before the label-processing control. Keep the existing path and extend the row's note to say: 'Add a rule with Content contains > Sensitivity labels and the Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content action.' The cited page's Supported conditions and actions table gives this condition/action pair.

claims.claim: The New-DLPCompliancePolicy and New-DLPComplianceRule calls use documented parameters and the Copilot content-processing block action.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The label-encryption path starts at the Purview portal and reaches Access control through the label scope and Control access selection.
claims.quote: Then, on the Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected page, make sure you select Control access.
claims.fix: The path is supported by this page together with the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels, but ends on the right page before the permission settings. Append ' > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now' to the current path, and append to the existing note: 'To set individual rights, select Assign permissions, add the intended recipients, then select Choose permissions.' Both steps are documented on the encryption page.
